1) 95th pct latency SLO target (you mentioned 800ms on the call — confirm)
2) Concurrent streams to support (target 50) and whether concurrency is per-user or global

4) Average tokens in request and response (if different)

I’ve looped Rafael (SE) and Aditya (Performance) on the next email to scope the sizing.

Hi all — quick technical write-up based on the sample traffic and the SLOs below. Attaching an SE sizing workbook (se-proposal-sizing.xlsx) and bench summary (bench-slides.png).

Summary of recommendation (short):
- Recommended POC: 2 x H100-80GB (reserved) with a burstable policy to add 1 additional H100 if peak sustained > 2x baseline during ramp tests.
- Alternate (lower cost): 4 x A100-80GB (reserved). H100 gives ~1.6-1.9x single-GPU streaming tail improvement in our in-house tests for the class of models you run (causal decoder, 8k context). See attached redwood-dedicated-bench-A100-vs-H100.pdf for details.

Sizing rationale (workload inputs):
- Traffic shape: baseline 25 rps, peak bursts to 60 rps; ~70% streaming average.
- Model: open-llama-65B (quantized to 4-bit perf profile we discussed).
- Average tokens: request 120, response 256 => avg output tokens per request ~256.
- Effective tokens/sec per stream (assuming 30 tokens/sec decode rate): ~8.5s to finish a response average; streaming means steady bandwidth on the decode path.

Empirical throughput/latency estimates (per-GPU, ballpark from our bench with similar model + config):
- H100-80GB (quantized): ~9-12 concurrent streaming sessions at 95th <= 800ms (with continuous KV cache hit and moderate batching enabled).
- A100-80GB (quantized): ~4-6 concurrent streaming sessions at 95th <= 800ms under the same conditions.

POC sizing math (to hit 50 concurrent streams at 95th <=800ms):
- Using conservative H100 per-GPU concurrency = 9 => need 6 GPUs to safely hit 50 with headroom; but because bursts are short and our runtime supports multi-GPU shared reserved throughput + autoscaling/burst, we recommend a 2 x H100 reserved pool + burst capacity (auto-burst to additional H100s) and configuration of reserved throughput to guarantee baseline SLA for 25 rps and allow burst scaling to 60 rps. This keeps committed cost lower while still meeting SLOs during normal operation.
- If customer requires hard reserved capacity to cover peak without bursting, recommend 6 x H100 or 12 x A100 (higher cost).

Streaming-specific notes:
- Keep prefix/KV cache warm for common prompts to reduce startup latency — we can provide an index of top prompt prefixes to pre-populate between tests.
- Continuous batching should be tuned to avoid increasing tail latency on streaming responses; we recommend low-latency batching windows (2–5ms) for this POC.

Next steps we propose:
1) Approve POC config: 2x H100 reserved + burst (SE will set autoscale policy).
2) Redwood to schedule 2-week POC window and run ramp tests (we’ll provide test harness and load driver).
3) Post-POC: if 95th tail meets their SLOs, we’ll produce a proposed committed capacity contract (monthly) with pricing.

Estimated timeline & cost (ballpark for POC):
- POC setup: 2–3 business days to provision and configure.
- Estimated incremental cost for 2-week POC (2x H100 reserved + burst allowance): ~USD 14k–18k (includes infra and priority SE time).

Peter / Kirsten — does this match expectations? If you want a firm quote for procurement I can convert this into a short SOW and formal pricing.

Thanks,
